=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- agents.d/7355-dead-values-cleanup.md:2 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The clause "`last_rebuild_at=none` means no earlier rebuild was recorded" is inaccurate. `_check_branch_rebuild_threshold` in scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh clears `BRANCH_REBUILD_LAST_REBUILD_AT` at line 11464 and sets it only at line 11536, after the earlier skip reasons: `disabled` (11468), `unsupported_branch` (11476), `missing_escalated_at` (11482), `invalid_current_time` (11493), `invalid_escalated_at` (11499), `threshold_not_met` (11506), `audit_unavailable` (11518), `invalid_audit_timestamp` (11530).
  WHY: All of those early exits leave the value empty, so the log prints `last_rebuild_at=none` even though the audit was never read. The log line is correct and only the documented meaning is wrong. The fix is to reword the clause to say that `none` means no earlier rebuild timestamp was read.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

- agents.d/7355-dead-values-cleanup.md:2 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fragment says `last_rebuild_at=none` means "no earlier rebuild was recorded," which is not always established by the check. `_check_branch_rebuild_threshold` clears `BRANCH_REBUILD_LAST_REBUILD_AT` at `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:11464` and can return before reading the audit, such as for `threshold_not_met` at lines 11504-11507.
  WHY: On an early return, the log emits `none` even if the audit contains a prior rebuild timestamp. Operators may wrongly conclude that no earlier rebuild was recorded, when its timestamp was only not read.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- agents.d/7355-dead-values-cleanup.md:2 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The phrase "`last_rebuild_at=none` means no earlier rebuild was recorded" is misleading. `BRANCH_REBUILD_LAST_REBUILD_AT` is cleared at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:11464 and set only at :11536 after the audit is read. For every earlier skip reason (disabled, unsupported_branch, missing_escalated_at, invalid_current_time, invalid_escalated_at, threshold_not_met, audit_unavailable), the audit is never consulted, so the log shows `none` because the audit was not read.
  WHY: Operators reading the contractual log documentation would wrongly conclude that no rebuild was ever recorded when they see `last_rebuild_at=none` for an early skip. The wording should clarify that `none` means the audit was not consulted or no timestamp was found.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
